title: Reorder List
oneLinerQuestion: Reorder a linked list to interleave nodes from the start and the end.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Reorder List problem asks us to reorder a singly linked list L_0 -> L_1 -> ... -> L_{n-1} -> L_n into the interleaved format L_0 -> L_n -> L_1 -> L_{n-1} -> L_2 -> L_{n-2} -> ... in-place without modifying node values. Because singly linked lists cannot be traversed backwards, pairing nodes from opposite ends requires access to the second half in reverse order. We can decompose the problem into three fundamental linked list primitives: locating the midpoint via two pointers, reversing the second half in-place, and interleaving (merging) the two independent halves alternately in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

- Step 1: Base Case & Edge Checking — If `head === null` or `head.next === null` or `head.next.next === null`, the list has fewer than three nodes and is already in reordered form, so we return immediately.

- Step 2: Locating the Middle Node — We deploy two pointers: `let slow = head` and `let fast = head`. While `fast.next !== null && fast.next.next !== null`, we advance `slow = slow.next` (1 step) and `fast = fast.next.next` (2 steps). When `fast` reaches the end, `slow` rests at the exact end of the first half.

- Step 3: Splitting the List — We decouple the two halves to prevent circular links: `let second = slow.next; slow.next = null`. Now the list is cleanly divided into a first half starting at `head` and a second half starting at `second`.

- Step 4: Reversing the Second Half In-Place — We reverse the second sublist using standard three-pointer iteration: `let prev = null, curr = second`. While `curr !== null`, we save `const nextTemp = curr.next`, point `curr.next = prev`, shift `prev = curr`, and advance `curr = nextTemp`. After completion, `prev` is the new head of the reversed second half.

- Step 5: Interleaving/Merging the Two Halves — We initialize two running pointers: `let first = head` and `let second = prev`. While `second !== null`, we cache their upcoming nodes (`const temp1 = first.next`, `const temp2 = second.next`), redirect pointers to weave them together (`first.next = second`, `second.next = temp1`), and advance both pointers forward (`first = temp1`, `second = temp2`).

- Step 6: Termination & In-Place Completion — Once `second` is fully consumed, all elements are successfully interleaved in-place, preserving the existing node references without returning a new head.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the total number of nodes, as finding the middle takes N/2 steps, reversing the second half takes N/2 steps, and interleaving takes N steps. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space because pointer manipulations are executed entirely in-place without allocating extra nodes or arrays.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION reorderList(head):
    slow = head, fast = head.next
    WHILE fast AND fast.next DO slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next
    second = slow.next; slow.next = NULL; prev = NULL
    WHILE second DO temp = second.next; second.next = prev; prev = second; second = temp
    first = head; second = prev
    WHILE second DO
        t1 = first.next, t2 = second.next
        first.next = second; second.next = t1
        first = t1; second = t2
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION

Line 3: Advance slow by 1 (to node 2) and fast by 2 (to node 4).

Line 4: Split list at slow. Set second = slow.next (4), then disconnect slow.next = NULL.
Line 5: Phase 2: Reverse second half. Point node 4 backward: 4 -> NULL, prev = 4, second = 5.
Line 5: Reverse node 5: 5 -> 4. Reversed second half complete: [5 -> 4].
Line 6: Phase 3: Prepare interleave. Set first = head (1), second = prev (5).
Lines 8-9: Link first (1) -> second (5). Advance first to t1 (2).
Lines 8-9: Link second (5) -> next first node (2). Partial chain: 1 -> 5 -> 2.
Lines 8-9: Link node 2 -> node 4, then link node 4 -> remaining node 3.
Line 12: second pointer reached NULL. Reorder completed in-place: 1 -> 5 -> 2 -> 4 -> 3.
